```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
options(digits=2)
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
require(lubridate)
kRdata <- read.csv(file = 'kRdata.csv')
kRdata <- kRdata %>%
mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))
kData = kRdata
```
Data are from the Patient_Info dataset from South Korea 1 Jan to 1 May 2020. These data were retrieved from a downloadable zip file from kaggle.

Some of the data were uncoded for sex - sex must be just male or female.  77 of the data entries were coded sex as blank, so we omit these.  State of a patient must be died or alive - we adjust that as well.  This is done in the mutate function. 

Variables of interest: sex, result

Research Question: - Is dying independent of sex?

# Introduction  

We will determine if sex, either being a Man or Women is a factor in living or dying of Covid19?  Using the KData,from the Patient_Info dataset that was retrieved from a downloadable dataset on Kaggle. which contains Covid19 patient information from South Korea between January 1 and May 1, 2020. The purpose of this analysis is to examine whether a relationship exists between a patient's sex and their outcome from COVID-19.

$H_0$ Dying and sex are independent. There is no relationship between a patient's sex and whether they died from COVID-19 in South Korea in 2019.

$H_A$ Dying and sex are not independent. There is a relationship between a patient's sex and whether they died from COVID-19 in South Korea in 2019.  

# Methods  

Sex, if Women or Man is a Categorical variable. 

Result, whether living or deceased is categorical.

# Data Results

## Graphical results  

```{r}
barchartGC(~result + sex ,data=kData)
barchartGC(~result + sex,data=kData, type="percent")

```  
The graph suggests that males are likely to die

## Numerical results  

```{r}
table1 <- xtabs(~result + Sex, data=kData)
rowPerc(table1)
colPerc(table1)
```
The numerical results shows that 64% of males died compared to 36% of females, indicating that men are almost twice as likely to die than women.  

## Inferential results  

```{r}
chisq.test(table1)
chisqtestGC(table1)
fisher.test(table1)
```  

The P-Value is 0.001, which is less than 0.05. This means that we reject the null hypothesis.We conclude that there is a connection between sex and death from Covid19.
